## For each feature: exact Overview, Role Lens, Behavior, states, edge cases, and end-to-end examples

### Feature: Credit-Backed Portfolio > Role Lens
## Role Lens

| Role | Access | What They See/Do |
|------|--------|-------------------|
| Musician | Full | Their portfolio assembles itself from credits others gave them. They control emphasis and grouping (`02.01.02`'s pins + ≤3 primary role families), never content. **Their own view is the only complete one** — it is the only place their `Confidential` ghost-production credits, embargoed sessions, Unlisted lines and rung-1 imports all appear at once, each marked with why it is invisible to everyone else (`02.01.05` D-09). Their pain — "every new client requires re-proving who they are and what they've played on" — ends here: the proof is standing, cited, and someone else supplied it. Their public human-level page aggregates only the aliases they have publicly linked (01.01.02 D-07); the rest of their career is theirs alone to see. |
| Producer | Full | Same on their own portfolio; they are also its largest *supplier* — every session they capture builds someone else's. This is the double role that makes the graph grow: the trust broker's attestation is worth more than a self-claim, so their capture creates value for people who are not them. **The specific bite for them**: their own solo work is structurally capped at rung 4 forever (`02.04.02` D-08, Q-04) — there is nobody independent to confirm a one-person session, so the persona that supplies everyone else's corroboration cannot obtain their own. |
| Operator | Read-only | Reads portfolios to decide bookings — "has this band actually played rooms this size?" — which is exactly what makes the artifact worth having. Their **room's own** portfolio is a portfolio in the same sense, with one hard limit inherited from `02.01.02` D-05: it lists works + the room's own credit role + the work's public primary artist, and **never the contributor roster**, because a roster is a client list and a room that leaks its client list loses its clients. They read every portfolio through a phone at a loading dock (`personas.md`). |
| Fan | Read-only | Browses it as discovery: what has this artist played on, who did they play with. Sees a plain-language evidence sentence — "Confirmed by 3 people who were there" — with **no rung name, no attester identity, no session metadata, no timestamps** (`02.04.02` D-04). Follow only; never a contact control (`02.01.02` D-11). The fan is why the portfolio must be legible without industry literacy — the same artifact serving a booker and a curious listener. |

> **Access levels**: Full · Config · Read-only · Reports · None

### Feature: Credit-Backed Portfolio > Decisions (2)
| # | Decision | Context |
|---|----------|---------|
| D-01 | The subject cannot edit their portfolio's content — only emphasis and grouping (`02.01.02`'s pins + ≤3 primary role families) | DT-01 — an editable portfolio is a claim, and claims are what the platform exists to replace |
| D-02 | **Evidence class and count publish; attester identity never does — at any tier, to any viewer.** Co-contributors are public (a collaborator is not an attester) | **Corrects the breadth pass** (DT-05). Publishing the attester hands a scraper the moat (`02.01.02` DT-04), turns a private act into a public endorsement, and buys nothing the evidence sentence does not already carry (`02.04.02` D-04) |
| D-03 | The portfolio is a view over the credit graph, never a stored document | A stored copy could drift from the graph, and the graph is the evidence. Same finding as `02.01.02` ("a discography is a query, not a document") |
| D-04 | It renders for unclaimed parties | Parent D-03 — the growth loop's bait. **Conditional on D-08**, per DT-09 |
| D-05 | **Uncorroborated credits render marked; contested credits render unmarked.** A rung is evidence and publishes; a contest is an objection and does not | **Corrects the breadth pass** (DT-06), adopting `02.01.02` D-06. The inherited `02.05` D-02 ↔ `02.01.02` D-06 contradiction is **closed, not open**: `02.04.02` Q-06 is resolved and `02.05` D-02 now marks for participants and never suppresses, matching `02.01.02` D-06 and credits-attribution CX-16. This row therefore inherits a settled rule |
| D-06 | **The portfolio never claims completeness, and never renders chronological density on a public surface** — no activity graph, no per-year counts, no timeline spine. A range is a fact; a timeline invites gap-reading | DT-07. The platform manufactures the gaps itself via embargo, and the subject cannot explain one without breaching the NDA that caused it. Independently forced by `02.01.05` D-05 |
| D-07 | **The human-level portfolio aggregates only publicly-linked aliases, and every derived fact — scalars and collaborator edges — is computed over the visible set, never filtered from the complete one** | DT-10, resolving domain CX-04. Per 01.01.02 D-07. Testable invariant: nothing derived from a privately-linked alias may vary observably on the public portfolio |
| D-08 | **An unclaimed party's portfolio requires an account-free remedy path** — "not you? / this credit is wrong" with no signup | DT-09. The bait is a publication about a non-consenting human; accountability without remedy is not enough. Reuses the no-login surface `01.06.03` D-03 already requires |
| D-09 | **A merge re-evaluates alias linkage visibility per alias**, never inheriting the survivor's | DT-13. The exact analogue of `02.01.05` D-17 for confidentiality. Linkage is reversible; disclosure is not |
| D-10 | **No party-level aggregate score on the portfolio, ever** | `02.04.02` D-14, honoured here because this is where the pull is strongest — a service

### Feature: Profile Page Composition > Deep Think Annotations (2)
| # | Hypothesis | Source | Outcome |
|---|-----------|--------|---------|
| DT-01 | The profile is a presentation layer over other domains' data, therefore not a real feature | The strongest argument against this sub-domain — a verifier already used a version of it against the whole domain | ❌ REJECTED — the domain overview settles the destination question ("the most-visited page type... the artifact hiring decisions are made from"), but there is a better reason. The page is where the platform *decides what verified means* to a stranger in eight seconds. That decision cannot live in 02 (which knows credits but not the person's other four facets) or in 16 (which knows rooms but not reputations). Composition is the only place the whole party is visible at once, and it is a product decision, not a rendering one. |
| DT-02 | Users should have rich composition control | The creator-platform instinct — musicians are expressive people and will want it | ⏳ SPLIT — control over *asserted* sections, none over *attested* ones. The distinction is the feature. A page where the subject can edit their credits is a Linktree with extra steps, and every competitor already has one. The value is precisely that some of the page is not theirs to write. How much control over the rest is a design question (parent Q-03) — but the line itself is not negotiable. **Sharpened by DT-06**: the line is not drawn between sections, it is drawn between facts. |
| DT-03 | The visual distinction between asserted and attested content is the platform's entire differentiator, expressed in a layout decision | Reasoning from `personas.md`: the Musician's success criterion is "credits are **cited** rather than claimed" — that word is doing a lot of work | ✅ CONFIRMED, and it is a constraint on `/create-prd-design-system`, not just this file. If a self-written bio and an attested credit render with the same visual weight, the platform has spent its whole thesis on a page that looks like every other music profile. The distinction has to be legible to a stranger who has never heard of us and will not read a legend. Nobody in the sweep named this; it is the point at which provenance either becomes visible or does not. |
| DT-04 | The page should adapt to its viewer — show a booker the credits, show a fan the shows | The obvious fix for the venue's two-audience problem (Q-03), and every personalisation instinct in modern product design | ❌ REJECTED, and the rejection produced the better answer. Three fatal objections. (1) **A page that renders differently per viewer is not a credibility artifact** — "I saw X on your page" stops being checkable, two bookers comparing notes see…

…mes misleading. For a *provenance* platform this is self-harm. (2) **The stranger has no signal** — the highest-value visitor is a promoter with no account (01.06.03 DT-03), so adaptation would work worst exactly where the page matters most. (3) It is **unnecessary**, which is the interesting part: D-03 already derives se…

| Scenario | What Happens | User Sees |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Empty profile — new user, no credits, no history | Honest emptiness. Not a fake-full page, not a completion meter (D-11). The empty state's job is to point at the one action that fills it — and the honest fact is that **someone else** has to act | A near-empty page and one route to the first real fact ("Your credits appear here when someone you've worked with adds them.") |
| **Multi-hyphenate with five facets** | **RESOLVED (D-07)** — the record is one filtered chronology; role is a property of each credit, not a section header. Filter chips derive from facets with evidence. The detail layer sections per facet, because its fields are heterogeneous. A primary role is neither needed nor introduced (01.01.01 D-01 intact) | One list of work with role shown per item; chips: `All · Production · Drums · Mixing`. Default chip is the subject's emphasis; every other chip is one tap away |
| Multi-hyphenate whose facets have **no evidence yet** (asserts `teacher`, has never taught) | No filter chip — chips derive from facets **with evidence**, so an empty chip is never rendered (D-03). The descriptor still renders in the header. The claim shows; the empty section does not | Header says "guitar tutor"; the record has no Teaching chip and no empty Teaching section |
| Facet whose domain has not shipped yet (`teacher` before 06 is live) | Identical to the row above, for a different reason and with the same answer. 01.01.01 D-13 keeps the claim assertable; D-03 keeps the section absent | Descriptor renders; no section; no "coming soon" placeholder occupying the page |
| Party is unclaimed but rich (a shadow with 30 credits) | Renders fully, marked unclaimed. Deliberate — this is the claim incentive (parent D-03, domain CX-04) | "This profile hasn't been claimed. Is this you?" |
| **The unclaimed page has no asserted layer at all** | Structural, and worth stating: nobody has spoken for this party. The page is **100% other people's word** — the purest expression of the thesis, and exactly why it is good bait. Even the Header is creator-asserted (a Producer typed "Sam — horn"), marked with its creator (01.05.01 D-03) | "Added by Sam Reeves" on the header. On claim, the asserted layer appears — empty — and the claimant may correct the name (matching 01.05.02's inheritance pattern: "remove it if that's not you") |
| An unclaimed party wants a false fact corrected but will not create an account | **The correction route must not require a claim (D-17).** Requiring a stranger to register in order to remove untrue claims the platform published about them is coercive, and it converts a growth loop into a hostage situation. Adjudication is 24's; the route's existence is this page's | A correction/removal route on the page itself, not behind the claim flow. Statutory thresholds: Q-06 |
| Subject dislikes an attested fact (a credit on a record they would rather forget) | Cannot delete it — it …

## For each feature: every Deep Think DT-* hypothesis and outcome exact text

### Feature: EPK Generation & Sharing > Deep Think Annotations
## Deep Think Annotations

| # | Hypothesis | Source | Outcome |
|---|-----------|--------|---------|
| DT-01 | An EPK is a document you export | The universal current practice — a PDF one-sheet, which `personas.md` explicitly lists as the Musician's workaround | ❌ REJECTED as the *model*, though possibly required as an output (Q-02). A document is stale on export and its credits are the artist's word. A view is current and its credits are the graph's. But the recipient — a promoter in an email thread — may simply not accept a link, which is why rejecting the model does not settle the artifact. Model and format are separate decisions. |
| DT-02 | One EPK per artist | How every EPK tool works | ❌ REJECTED — an EPK is an *argument*, and the argument differs by recipient. A festival slot pitch, a sync brief and a label pitch need different emphases and different credits foregrounded. One EPK means one argument, which means a generic one, which is why every hand-built EPK is mediocre. Per-pitch generation is nearly free once the facts are already held — which is the whole advantage of generating rather than authoring. |
| DT-03 | The EPK is where the platform's value becomes legible to people who are not users | Reasoning about who actually reads it: the promoter is not our user and may never be | ✅ CONFIRMED, and it changes the feature's strategic weight. The EPK is a **distribution surface**, not a convenience: it is a WeJammin artifact that lands in the inbox of every promoter, label and supervisor its users pitch — people who have never heard of us. Each one shows attested credits they cannot get anywhere else, and every one of those promoters is a future Operator claim (01.05.02). The EPK is the domain's outbound growth loop the way shadow parties are its inbound one. Nobody in the sweep named this, and it argues the artifact must work *perfectly for a stranger with no account, on a phone*. |
| DT-04 | A sent EPK should snapshot at send time to protect the sender from the pitch changing under them (Q-01) | The obvious fix for the "what was pitched ≠ what is now seen" hazard | ❌ REJECTED. Snapshotting freezes the attested credits into a static claim — which is exactly a PDF, and forfeits the live-view advantage that is the whole reason to generate rather than author. The real risk is not that the recipient sees *new* truth (they should); it is that the sender is *unaware* the pitch changed. So the fix is a **sent-state watch on the sender's side**: keep the view live, notify the sender when a foregrounded fact materially changes. The recipient always sees current truth; the sender is never surprised. This resolves Q-01 without reintroducing staleness. |

### Feature: Credit-Backed Portfolio > Deep Think Annotations (2)
| # | Hypothesis | Source | Outcome |
|---|-----------|--------|---------|
| DT-01 | A portfolio is a thing you build | Every portfolio product ever made — SoundBetter, LinkedIn, a PDF one-sheet, a Linktree | ❌ REJECTED, and the rejection is the feature. A self-built portfolio is a claim, and `problem-statement.md` says the industry's whole failure is that "they are asking people to remember" — a self-built portfolio asks people to *assert*, which is worse. Making it unbuildable-by-its-subject is the only thing here a competitor cannot copy: Jaxsta and Muso.AI can ingest liner notes, but they cannot make the producer who ran the session attest on the day, because they were not in the room. |
| DT-02 | A credit is binary — you have it or you don't | The obvious model, and how every credits database works | ❌ REJECTED — a credit's value is a function of the evidence behind it. `personas.md` calls the Producer a trust broker whose attestation "is worth more than a self-claim, which is precisely what makes counter-attestation valuable". A binary credit throws that away and hands the anti-persona a free reputation machine. Confidence must be legible on the face of the portfolio, not buried in a detail view — which `02.04.02` D-02 confirms independently and specifies as a 6-rung ladder. **Amended by DT-05**: legible ≠ attributed. |
| DT-03 | The portfolio's greatest weakness is that it cannot hold the past, and this is the adoption problem in one artifact | Reasoning about the veteran's case: a 20-year session player's page is emptier than a newcomer's who did one session last week | ✅ CONFIRMED as the problem; **mechanism resolved by a peer this pass.** `02.03.01` had already answered it while this file was still asking: import at rung 1, permanently source-marked, never promotable — "gravity, never evidence" (`02.03.01` DT-01). The purity survives because the rung survives. What does not resolve is the product judgment (Q-01), and `02.01.02` DT-06 independently reached the sharper form: the page's biggest lie is omission, so it must never present as a résumé. Two features found the same wound from opposite sides, which is the strongest evidence it is real. |
| DT-04 | 01.06.02 and `02.01.02` Public Discography are the same feature wearing two names, and one of them should not exist | Adversarial, and the strongest argument against this file. Both describe "a party's credits, rendered, with provenance visible". `02.01.02` is `[DEEP]` and specifies grouping, bounds, pins, archive, counts, merges and rate limits — leaving this file apparently holding an empty noun | ⚠️ **CONFIRMED as a severe overlap, REJECTED as a duplication — and the resolution is a word.** `02.01.02` renders a **party**. An alias is a party; a Band is a…

## For each feature: every Open Question exact text, owner, Deferred To, and what it blocks

### Feature: Credit-Backed Portfolio > Open Questions
## Open Questions

| # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
|---|----------|-------|-------------|
| Q-01 | **[OWNER] Is import-for-gravity enough for the veteran, or does the product owe them something else?** — *narrowed, not open.* The mechanism is settled: imports render at rung 1, permanently source-marked, never promotable (`02.03.01` D-01, `02.04.02` D-03), and no copy claims completeness (D-06). The residue is a product judgment: does a page reading "1,847 credits — Listed on Discogs" help a 20-year veteran or advertise that the platform did not witness their career? The alternatives all fail — retroactive attestation is reconstruction (`02.04.02` DT-06), self-assertion is rung 2, and contemporaneity is unbackfillable by physics (`02.04.02` DT-10). **Recommendation: accept it and fix the copy, and move import earlier in `/plan-phase`** — the honest answer is the only available one, and its cost is entirely in framing. A framing judgment about what the product owes a persona; the domain index already carries it as `[OWNER]` Q-05 pointed at `/create-prd` (01.06.02 Q-01). (DT-03; domain-index Q-05.) | User | `/create-prd` |
| Q-02 | **What identity strength must a claimed account reach before its attestation counts?** — *reframed by DT-08.* The breadth-pass question (can two shadows attest each other) is closed: they cannot, because a shadow is a subject and never an agent (01.05.01 D-05). What remains is real and unowned: `02.04.02` states plainly that it has **no defence against sockpuppets and does not claim one** — independence is per human (D-08/DT-17), so the tier model's integrity rests entirely on this domain. Contemporaneity caps the payoff (a ring buys a future, never a career) but does not close it. The question is identity's to answer and 02 cannot. **Sharpened by DQ-06.1/DQ-06.2 (D-12)**: ring detection now exists but is **score-only**, so it moves nothing this page renders and nothing any rung gate reads. Identity strength is therefore not merely the tier model's *primary* defence — for everything the public portfolio shows, it is the **only** one. | Agent | `/create-prd-security` |
| Q-03 | **[OWNER] May a downstream domain filter candidates on provenance rung?** A tier floor inside one party's archive is harmless (`02.01.02`); the same filter across the marketplace excludes every solo creator from being hired, because `02.04.02` Q-04 caps them at rung 4 forever for a property of their working method rather than their competence. Neither 04 nor 05 has any reason to notice. **Recommendation: no marketplace-wide rung floor** — the portfolio supplies a signal, and turning an honest epistemics into an employment gate would make the platform's differentiator a barrier against a large and growing population. (DT-11.) **Not settled by 02**: credits-attribution index D-11 leaves "out-of-domain rung gates" to each consuming domain, and ideation-cx 01-05 already carries the recommendation ("no aggregate score, no marketplace-wide rung flo

### Feature: EPK Generation & Sharing > Open Questions
## Open Questions

| # | Question | Owner | Deferred To |
|---|----------|-------|-------------|
| Q-01 | ✅ RESOLVED (Step 5, D-05/DT-04): stay **live**, never snapshot; a send watches the foregrounded facts and notifies the sender on material change. Recipient always sees current truth; sender is never surprised by a pitch that changed under them. | — | Resolved |

### Feature: Profile Page Composition > Behavior > States
### States

| State | Trigger | What User Sees |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| Loading | Page fetch | Header resolves first and independently; lower layers render section-level skeletons. A skeleton is only shown where a section is known to exist — an absent section must never flash in and out |
| Empty | No facts yet, no asserted content | Honest empty page: header, and one route to a real fact. No scaffolding, no completion meter (D-11), no invented sections |
| Populated | Facts accrued | The four-layer spine, with every fact carrying its provenance state (D-05) and the attested treatment legible to a stranger with no legend (D-02) |
| Error | Fetch failed | Error with retry. **Never renders a partial page as complete**, and never renders a failed section as absent (D-12) — on this page absence means "no data exists", so an error rendered as absence is a factual claim the platform did not intend to make |
| Partial | Some layers resolved, the record still resolving | Section-level skeletons in the unresolved layers; resolved layers are usable. Never a page that looks finished while its best content is missing |
| Unclaimed | Party created by reference (01.05.01), no owner | The record renders in full; the asserted layer does not exist because nobody has spoken. The header is creator-asserted and names its creator. A claim affordance fronts the page; a correction route sits beside it and does not require claiming (D-17) |
| Frozen | Party deceased (01.10) | Legacy treatment. Facets and asserted content read-only; a marked estate notice may be added; the record is untouched and permanent |

## Credit-Backed Portfolio forced decisions an implementer must invent despite cited decisions

### Feature: Credit-Backed Portfolio > Behavior > What publishes and what does not
### What publishes and what does not

This is the feature's load-bearing rule, and the breadth pass got it wrong.

| Element | Publishes? | Source |
|---|---|---|
| The claim — party, role, work | ✅ Yes | Liner notes are public by nature (`02.01.02` DT-04) |
| The evidence **class and count** — "Confirmed by 3 people who were there" | ✅ Yes | `02.04.02` D-02, D-04 |
| The rung label (professional viewer) | ✅ Yes | `02.01.02` D-02 |
| **Attester identity** | ❌ **Never, at any tier, to any viewer including authenticated professionals** | `02.01.02` DT-04 |
| Session metadata, capture timestamps, capture origin, traversal paths | ❌ Never | `02.01.02` DT-04 |
| A contested marker | ❌ Never publicly | `02.01.02` D-06 |
| A party-level aggregate score ("94% verified") | ❌ **Never. There is no party-level tier** | `02.04.02` D-14 |
| A platform-behaviour statistic (capture rate, session count, response time) | ❌ Never | `02.01.02` D-10 |
| Per-year credit density / activity timeline | ❌ **Never** (D-06, DT-07) | This file; forced by `02.01.05` D-05 |

**Co-contributors are not attesters, and the distinction is what saves the feature.** The portfolio publishes who the subject *worked with* — that is a credit on a shared work, public by nature, and walking it is the point (`02.01.03`). It never publishes who *vouched for* the subject. Everyone on the roll is a collaborator; only some of them attested. Conflating the two would put a private, socially-costly act on a public page and hand a scraper the evidence trail that is the entire moat.

**"Cited rather than claimed" survives this.** The booker does not need the citer's name; they need to know that independent co-present confirmation exists and how much. That is what the evidence sentence carries. The breadth pass conflated *cited* with *the citation is signed in public* — they are different, and only the first is defensible.

| **The portfolio as a projection onto a *human identity* rather than onto a party** | **This file** | Owner. |
| **The portfolio as the attested half of a composed profile** (01.06.01's asserted/attested line) | **This file** | Owner. |
| **The portfolio of a party that does not yet have an owner** (claim bait, and its liability) | **This file** | Owner. |

The seam is the word **party**. `02.01.02` renders one party's page — and an alias *is* a party (01.01.02 D-01/D-02), a Band *is* a party, a room *is* a party. A **human** is not: their career is spread across aliases that `02.01.02` renders as strangers to each other. Nothing in domain 02 aggregates a human, because domain 02 does not know which parties are one person — that fact lives in identity (01.01.02 D-07), and it is privacy-governed.

So: **02 owns the party's discography. 01.06.02 owns the identity's portfolio.** Where they touch the same pixels, 02's `[DEEP]` decisions win and this file cites them.

### Feature: Credit-Backed Portfolio > Overview
## Overview

The body of work behind a party, assembled from what other people attested rather than from what its subject typed. Every credit in it was supplied by someone who was in the room — a producer who ran the session, a bandmate, a venue that hosted it — and the subject cannot edit any of it. This is `personas.md`'s success criterion made concrete: **credits are cited rather than claimed**.

> **Deep Think addition (split)** — the sweep's candidate bundled portfolio into "Portfolio, Media Reel & EPK" as a presentational concern. Splitting it out is deliberate: a portfolio nobody can edit is a different product from a portfolio its owner writes, and it is the only asset here a competitor cannot manufacture retroactively.

### Feature: Profile Page Composition > Behavior > The unit of provenance is the fact, not the section
### The unit of provenance is the fact, not the section

The breadth pass said sections divide into **asserted** (bio, photos, links, rates — the subject wrote them) and **attested** (credits, collaborators, shows played, badges — other parties supplied them). The division is right; the **granularity was wrong**, and two ratified upstream decisions already prove it:

- **01.02.01 D-06** — an org attribute "may carry **counterparty confirmations** alongside the org's own assertion". A venue's asserted 120-capacity claim, confirmed by twelve bands who played it, is one fact with two provenance layers. It is not an asserted section and not an attested section.
- **The reel** (DT-07) — an asserted *selection* of clips over *attested* works. The subject chose the 30 seconds; the graph says they were on the record.

So: **provenance is a property of every fact; a section is only a container, and a section may mix.** Every fact on the page renders with its own provenance state:

| Provenance state | Meaning | Who can change the fact |
|---|---|---|
| **Asserted** | The subject said it | The subject |
| **Attested** | A named other party said it, on the record, at the time | Nobody on this page — only the attester, via domain 02 |
| **Confirmed-assertion** | The subject said it; named counterparties corroborated it (01.02.01 D-06) | The subject owns the claim; the confirmations are not theirs to add or remove |
| **Creator-asserted** | A third party said it about an unclaimed party who has never spoken (01.05.01) | The creator, until claim; then the claimant |
| **Disputed** | Attested, then contested (01.06.02 D-05) | Nobody — and the state is **not published**: the public line renders unchanged at its existing rung with **no contested marker** (`02.01.02` D-06; `02.01.01` D-11; 01.06.02 D-05). Never hidden, never dropped; the marker is a record-view affordance for the participants and the credited party only |

D-01 is unchanged and unweakened: **the subject cannot edit attested content.** What D-05 adds is that "attested" is a per-fact state, so a subject editing their capacity claim does not touch the twelve confirmations attached to it, and a section is never wholesale one thing or the other.

The visual distinction between these states must survive every layout decision downstream (D-02). A page where a self-claimed credit looks identical to an attested one has thrown away the platform's only structural advantage.

### Feature: EPK Generation & Sharing > Role Lens
## Role Lens

| Role | Access | What They See/Do |
|------|--------|-------------------|
| Musician | Full | Generates an EPK for a specific pitch — a festival, a support slot, a sync brief — with the emphasis that pitch needs. Sends it. Sees whether it was opened, which is the difference between silence and information. The credits section is the part they never have to write or update. |
| Producer | Full | Generates a client-facing kit: discography, room, rates, turnaround, testimonials. Their pitch is a service sale, not a booking, so the same generator serves a different argument. |
| Operator | Read-only | The primary **recipient**. They receive EPKs when booking and are the reason the artifact exists — so the design constraint is theirs: `personas.md` puts them on a phone at a loading dock, not at a desk. An EPK that needs a big screen and a PDF reader fails its actual audience. They also send the inverse artifact (a tech pack), which is domain 18's. |
| Fan | None | An EPK is a B2B artifact. A fan gets the public profile — which is a better, livelier surface for them anyway. Explicit absence: showing fans an EPK would be showing them a sales document about a person they already like. |
